evals.prompt: Run /theme-forge init in the current project for a bilingual English and Arabic furniture storefront called Cedar & Loom. Use the slug cedar-loom, support English and Arabic with RTL for Arabic, and create the theme-embedded design-first prototype structure (.design/ and .docs/) and documentation directly in the Shopify theme directory.
evals.expected_output: A preserved or newly created theme-embedded design workspace (.design/) with the default page prototypes represented, .docs/theme-settings.md containing the identity and 9-category global settings contract, .shopifyignore configured for .design/ and .docs/ paths, and AGENTS.md with a CLAUDE.md symbolic link instructing agents on the theme design system. The report identifies created, updated, skipped, and unresolved items.

evals.prompt: Run /theme-forge init-agents against this existing Shopify theme project. Inspect the workspace and generate or refresh AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md informing agents of the theme design contract in .design/ and .docs/ (tokenized CSS, zero hardcoded colors, OOP JavaScript, single stylesheet, single shell) and how to implement it across Liquid theme files without modifying or resetting existing design or theme files.
evals.expected_output: An inspected existing project where AGENTS.md is created or updated with complete theme-aware design guidance referencing .design/ and .docs/, CLAUDE.md is linked via symlink, .shopifyignore is configured, and no existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, fixture, or Liquid files are altered. A created/updated/skipped/unresolved completion report is output.

evals.prompt: I want to use Theme Forge for a storefront design prototype in my Shopify theme, but I have not said whether to initialize a new embedded prototype, configure agent guidance for an existing theme, or resolve/migrate a project. What should I do next? Do not inspect or change files yet.
evals.expected_output: A concise explanation of /theme-forge init, /theme-forge init-agents (or /theme-forge agents), and /theme-forge resolve, followed by a question asking the user to choose one. No files are created or modified.

evals.prompt: Run /theme-forge resolve in the current project to migrate any legacy standalone design folders (design/, docs/) into the theme-embedded structure (.design/, .docs/) and audit/reconcile our prototype against the latest skill rules: replace all hardcoded colors in .design/styles.css with semantic CSS custom properties, refactor procedural scripts in .design/script.js into ES6 OOP classes with a component registry, strip duplicate header/footer markup from secondary HTML pages to maintain a single shell in .design/index.html, ensure RTL logical properties, and synchronize .docs/theme-settings.md.
evals.expected_output: An audited, migrated, and reconciled theme prototype workspace where legacy standalone directories (if present) are converted to .design/ and .docs/, hardcoded colors in .design/styles.css are converted to semantic tokens across color schemes, JS in .design/script.js is refactored into ES6 OOP classes with lifecycles and a central registry, duplicate headers/footers in secondary HTML pages are stripped leaving only clean main content, logical CSS properties are enforced, .docs/theme-settings.md is synchronized, AGENTS.md is updated, and a detailed completion report is provided.

evals.prompt: Run /theme-forge init in an empty folder or a repository that has no Shopify theme structure (no layout/, templates/, sections/, snippets/, or config/). How should the skill respond?
evals.expected_output: The skill inspects the workspace, detects no Shopify theme structure, halts execution immediately without asking theme questions or creating .design/, .docs/, AGENTS.md, or .shopifyignore files, and outputs a clear error explaining that Theme Forge requires an existing Shopify theme directory with guidance on scaffolding a theme via Shopify CLI (`shopify theme init`).
